t: You're at Fitzroy Square, a Georgian square and the only one in the part of central London known as Fitzrovia. The district took its name from here, though the nearby Fitzroy Tavern probably had as much influence. The square is named for Henry FitzRoy, first Duke of Grafton, an illegitimate son of Charles the Second, who was killed at the storming of Cork in 1690. The artist and inventor Adelaide Claxton and the painter Marian Emma Chase were both born here. Sir George Buchanan, Chief Medical Officer, and Winifred Austin, a pioneer of library services for blind people, died here.
